Entry: Best day ever!!!
Scan was clear. Breathing.
Hoping the new medication helps Dad's confusion. Doctor says give it a month.
Raging at the bank. They closed my account with no warning and my salary bounced.
Finished my first full week as a carer on my own rounds. Twelve clients, everyone fed and safe. Not bad.
Wondering whether my art is any good or whether I just like making it. Maybe that's enough.
Dr. Banerjee wants to 'discuss the results in person'. Appointment isn't until Tuesday.
The team threw me a surprise send-off. Speeches, a card everyone signed, Wendy cried. I didn't know I mattered this much here.
My research participant cancelled for the fourth time and the ethics deadline is next week.
Twins in hospital with bronchiolitis, Grandma visiting from abroad, work threatening a disciplinary. I don't know which way is up.
history homework: done. room: tidy. me: suspiciously functional
I'm proud of how I handled Kian's meltdown in the supermarket. Stayed calm, knelt down, waited it out.
Nadia called to say the biopsy was benign. I've been holding my breath for two weeks.
Tidy flat, finished work, nice weather, and I still feel sad. Weird and annoying.
It was a day. Some good bits, some bad bits, nothing big either way.
Small hope that the café reopens. Liked that place.
Passed my driving test!!! Third time lucky. Dad honked the horn all the way down our street.
Spent the afternoon at the cemetery tidying Mum's grave. Planted primroses. Talked to her for a while about the kids. It was peaceful, not sad.
The rescue dog took a treat from my hand today instead of from the floor.
Hay's in before the rain. Whole family on the trailer. Sat on the bales after with cider.
Wonderful, the school wants a costume for World Book Day tomorrow. Told us at 8pm. Love that.
Two hours until the baby arrives by C-section. We've waited six years for this. I'm vibrating.
Two kids with the flu, me with the flu, nobody sleeping. Survival mode.
Fridge full, house warm, everyone asleep. Good night.
Sharma ji's son got into IIT and now the whole colony is comparing. Not stressed only, just tired of it.
Already packed. The trip is in nine days.
Idly wondering whether to change jobs one day.
Lake, quiet, me.
Hoping my brother's visa will be approved this time. Second application. Praying.
Results came out: B in chem! After failing the mocks I honestly thought I'd get a D. So happy.
First night in the empty house after Esi moved out. Even the fridge sounds loud.
I asked for one thing for my birthday: no drama. Dad brought drama.
Mum's surgery is at eight. They said four hours. I've cleaned the whole kitchen twice.
I keep forgetting things. Appointments, birthdays, why I walked into the room. Too much in my head.
The week from hell: car crash (minor, everyone's fine), work crisis, Babajide's hospital visit.
Swam a whole length without stopping. Learning at 45 is humbling and I did it.
Opened the letter from the hospital and read three paragraphs of words I didn't understand. Had to put it down.
Mild buzz about the weekend. Nothing big planned, just looking forward to it.
Wrote letters to all the grandchildren for their birthdays this year. Twelve of them. A whole afternoon. Satisfied.
Last day at the old school. Took one more photo of my classroom with the chairs up. Twelve years in that room.
Phoned the insurance about renewal. They'll email the quote.
Dad lost his job and now everything at home is tense. I'm trying to be invisible so I'm not another problem.
Thank you note to myself: you got through a hard month. You didn't quit.
What a joy, a 6am fire alarm drill in December. Everyone in pyjamas in the snow.
What a relaxing holiday: three flights, two delays, one lost passport and zero sleep.
Wiped out.
Got my driving licence at 52. Never too late.
Walked the same loop as always and still noticed new things. Life's good.
The doctor gave me so much information about the diagnosis I couldn't take any of it in.
The car is making the noise again. Can't afford a repair this month. Turning the radio up so I can't hear it.
Lovely, the car failed its MOT. On my birthday. Perfect timing as always.
My daughter stood up for a kid who was being picked on. The teacher called to tell me. I'm so proud of her.
Kids have all moved away. Big house. Quiet phone.
Quiet shift at the library. Shelved books, helped a kid find dinosaur books, drank too much tea. Nice.
Dad's in the care home now. I visit, but the house feels hollow without him in it.
Absolutely raging. The council towed my car from my own street because of a sign they put up yesterday.
Shared a pot of tea with Mrs. Hale next door and heard all about her roses. Lovely hour.
Tidied the desk, lit a candle, wrote three pages by hand. The world is far away tonight.
Grateful to the night bus driver who waited for me to run the last fifty metres.
Fixed the wobbly table with a folded receipt. Victory.
Love how the landlord 'fixed' the boiler by turning it off and on. Fourth cold shower this week. Living the dream.
Hope I can move to days soon. Doctor says the nights are hurting my sleep long-term.
Today I'm on edge for no clear reason. Snapped at the printer. Apologised to the printer.
Booked the holiday! Ten days off in August. First proper break in two years.
Sat in the garden and cried for a while about nothing in particular. Then I made soup.
Visited the new Ikea with Kostas. Bought a lamp and some storage boxes.
Started the new meds today. Doctor said the first week can be rough. Every little twinge I'm wondering if it's a side effect.
Lantern festival by the river. Thousands of little lights drifting. Everyone hushed.
Quiet. Settled. Fine.
Message from 'Unknown Number': 'Is this Sam?' It is not Sam. I am not Sam. Nobody here is Sam.
Grandkids arrive tomorrow! Baked three cakes. Don't tell their mother.
My twin is away for six months on the research ship. I didn't know quiet could be this loud.
Holding the urn felt wrong. It was so light. Dad was never light.
Yay, another wedding where I'm the only single one at the table. So much fun answering questions about it.

I sat down tonight to make a plan for the year, which I've been putting off since January. Instead of the usual list of goals I tried something Dr. Ortiz suggested: writing about what a good ordinary week would look like, not a perfect one. It turned out to be quite simple. Three runs. One dinner with friends. One evening completely on my own with a book. Calling Gran on Sundays. Work that I'm not ashamed of and home by seven most days. Enough sleep. Looking at it written down, almost none of it needs money or luck. It just needs me to say no to more things and protect the time. I feel quietly hopeful that this year could be the one where I stop chasing everything and start living in a way that actually suits me. It's a start.
Three exams in two days. Done. I want to sleep for a week.
Kept turning the old photo over in my hands. Same face, different person.
Content with the slow pace of village life. Post office, bakery, the pub quiz on Thursdays.
My manager noticed I was struggling and gave me the week off, paid. No questions.
Grateful for video calls. I am seeing my nephew grow even from far away.
I've stopped wanting a bigger house. This one has everything we need.
Church choir is doing the Messiah at Easter and I've got a solo. Terrified and thrilled.
Coach Brennan stayed after training to help me with my serve. Every week, for free. Legend.
Spent the day cataloguing the archive boxes. Boxes 14 to 22 done.
So angry I had to go for a walk before I said something I'd regret. Still angry after the walk.
Rained. Stayed in. Read.
Mum sent a voice note singing happy birthday off-key. Played it four times.
I notice I describe my week by what I achieved and never by how I felt. Trying to change the question.
New city, new job, no friends yet. Ate dinner watching other people's stories on my phone.
Toddler refused to nap, so I didn't either. Running on fumes.
The new software, the new process, the new manager. Too much change in one month.
I keep picturing the little house by the sea. One day. Saving towards it.
Trying to decide whether to do the nursing degree at 38. Scared I've left it too late. Writing it down to see how it looks.
Netflix raised the price again. Cancelled it. Spotify next probably.
So nice of Gavin to reply-all with my mistake to the entire company. What a team player.
Reviewing the year: hard, important, unexpectedly tender.
Iron levels are low, doctor says. Explains the constant fatigue. Starting supplements.
Lost my temper with my little brother and he cried. Felt horrible all evening. He's eight.
Lonely job, this. Driving all day, talking to satnav. The radio presenters feel like friends.
The young people at the bank were very patient today. Helped me set up the card on my phone. I'm quite modern now.
